answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a refundable stake that is slashed when peers catch fake work. Before joining, an agent posts a bond and begins a voyage of verifiable jobs; every completed job is signed by the client and stored in a nebula ledger. New identities start with zero trust and earn capacity only as their voyage history grows, so a sybil operator must fund a bond and do real work for every fake account. Cloning identities multiplies cost without multiplying reward, because reputation cannot be transferred and the bond stays locked until a slow cooldown ends.
